chapter: Los Angeles 1947-48, Rock Island and bebop in New York
title: Arrested at the train station: the commissary waitress, the reserved seat and the police c
summary: After a slight at the commissary, the conductor and police arrested Simmons, Shavers and Quebec; Quebec was clubbed.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah. Boy, that was a beautiful group. One of the best feelings I've had in a long time on a bandstand. One of the few, you know. Where you'd look forward to getting to work. Couldn't get to work fast enough, you know. Because every night someone was inventing something new and they were falling right in line. It was like ESP, reading one another's mind. Everybody knew what they was going to do, you know. It was a beautiful job, but I guess my mouth messed it up. As I said, Charlie was buying the tickets and I suggested to Ike, let's go over to the commissary and get some sandwiches. Well, the waitress there, she was busy, involved with a -- verbal conversations with the engineer, the fireman, the stoker, whoever he is that rides with the engineer. The pullman porters, the conductors, everyone but Ike and I. They're paying us no mind. Well, at this point I'm pretty irritated, you know. Ike's standing there. He's not showing any emotions whatsoever. So I blurted out what I thought, you know. Tell

that waitress so and so and so. And at that particular time, you could hear a pin drop on a piece of cotton, and nothing but my voice rang out. So I walked on out. Ike didn't know how to walk out. He was glued in his shoes. He finally came out. So we got on an empty car, and we picked out a seat for ourselves, and the conductor got on and he says, "You boys will have to change your seats." We said, "Why? It's an empty train. There's no-one on here but us. Why do we have to change our seats?" He said, "Well, this section here is reserved for the conductor," he says, "there's a plaque there." If you looked close enough. I looked back and sure enough, there was a brass plaque. But it was tarnished so it was the same color of the wall, you know, that was behind us. So we wasn't that observing that we saw the plaque when we sat there. Otherwise we wouldn't have sat there, you know. So we got up to move as he had complied, and in our moving, he saw this bottle of whiskey that Al Barnes had given us. He said, "You'll have to get rid of the whiskey before the train moves." I said, "Why?" I said, "We're not GIs, and the seal isn't broken on the bottle." "You'll still have to get rid of the bottle." I said, "Well, man, you --", and he says, "Let's get the niggers off the train." I said, "Oh, my God." I said, "Charlie, he's going after the police." Well, if you knew Charlie, and he laughed, he said, "Oh, no, man. Nothing like that." bubble eyes . Whiskey running out of his eyes, he's

so full of whiskey. He refuses to accept that. No sooner said than done. Here they come from both entrances. "All right, let's get off the train." I stand up, like Richard Pryor. "What's the charges, Officer?" Bam. Blackjack, right in the forehead. I ain't opening my mouth any more. I wasn't going to set the table for them to go any further. So we got out of the seats and started getting off the train, as ordered in the first place. So they handcuffed Ike to me, and they handcuffed Charlie singly and put him in one squad car and put Ike and I in another one. So I'm leading Ike into the back seat. I got in first. I'm pulling Ike behind me. And just as Ike bent over to get in the rear seat, this policeman got up on his toes with a billy club, what we call a night stick, trying to hit a home run, a la Mickey Mantle, Joe DiMaggio, Hank Aaron, say hey kid, Willie Mays, you know, with a tape measure. He hit this man so hard that blood just spouted everywhere. It was like a Texas T.

Right on the left rear part of his cranium, you know. And he got in the car and he's spouting blood all over the lapel of his overcoat. He said, "Look what he did to me, man." And I'm so disgusted, I say, "Yeah, he hit me, too, man. But he didn't strike blood." I'm real drug. So they take us to jail. Now, they've thrown the book at us. We are not aware of this at the time. They put us in jail.
